key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, environmentally stable planar silicon hybrid photovoltaics without substrate texturing.
method: Fabricate planar PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon.
Benchmark against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Evaluate optoelectronic performance and efficiency retention after 75 days of ambient exposure.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si, retaining approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 days versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish scalability or durability beyond 75 days; maintaining defect-free graphene coverage may be critical to barrier performance.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
